title: Browse authorized Case Timeline HTML from Command linked Incident without changing JSON API
goal: Make an actual human-readably navigable Class-0 Incident -> linked Case -> authorized Timeline browser journey using the already existing same-origin handlers and trusted owners. Content-negotiate escaped read-only HTML on the existing GET /case-timeline endpoint while preserving byte-for-byte the existing JSON schema and permission boundaries.
invariants: HTML is merely a representation of OpenCaseTimeline using existing distinct server-side Case, Timeline Entry and typed-source ownership; no read permission is accepted from request body, header or Command link.
An Incident.read or authorized Shared link is never promoted to Investigate Case.read; denied Case shows generic error, no HTML entries.
Existing JSON response is preserved when Accept begins application/json or is absent; existing API pagination/filter semantics remain intact.
For browser Accept text/html, default output is bounded to 50 of at most 5000 already authorized entries, or explicit validated limit at most 200; every page rechecks the complete owner/ACL chain.
Template escapes all source-controlled fields and uses no HTML/JS injected markup or new client-side runtime dependencies; strict CSP and no-store.
Older superseded versions are identified only from current independently authorized successor; missing flag cannot prove no hidden correction.
Page links include only validated case_id/filter/page selectors and never propagate bearer tokens, tenant, environment or permission decisions.
No new persistence, source owner, IAM, mutation, Query, Finding/Evidence, audit claim, or production deployment.
security_properties: Fail closed on malformed URI, invalid tenant/scope or denied Case before rendering; no partially written HTML on template error or canceled authorization context.
Content negotiation cannot change permissions or response contents before authorization.
HTML content uses html/template to escape IDs, types, times, provenance and source refs; never constructs links to unknown source owner endpoints.
No stale current-Case guarantee across multiple HTTP requests; visible pagination notice must indicate independently refreshed permission checks.

migration.rationale: New optional HTTP representation of existing read-only route, no API/schema storage change

rollback.strategy: Remove case_html.go and source-html branch, retaining exactly existing JSON handler and cross-product host
verification: All existing Case/Timeline and Command host tests unchanged

inputs: CAP-INV-110 Case Timeline §15 source, temporal uncertainty and correction status
Already implemented #199 source-owned Case Timeline, shared same-origin router and authorized linked Case href
outputs: A Command-initiated browser navigation now renders readable trusted Case Timeline HTML on the same /case-timeline route without requiring manual JSON inspection
Explicit supersession, original source, provenance, time uncertainty and page links produced only from owner-authorized values
Existing JSON client response remains unchanged; local HTTP synthetic owner fixture tests both forms
acceptance_tests: Following selected Command Incident's Case hyperlink with Accept:text/html goes through real first-party Command/Investigate Go handler composition and displays old/new authorized Timeline records and supersession on different pages
Command-only, missing/invalid tokens and foreign Case yield no HTML or entry/source disclosure
Direct Case handler produces <=50 rows by default and honors validated limit/offset; link to next page forces new independent owner checks
Source-controlled HTML metacharacters escaped, strict CSP and Cache-Control no-store, no inline script, no links to unauthorized source endpoints
Existing JSON response when requested by API client, full Go tests/vet/race on Linux/macOS/Windows and required engineering-kernel CI on exact SHA
definition_of_ready: CAP-INV-110 existing Class-0 timeline read requires a human-readable view and permitted correction/source metadata
E10-INV-110F-SUPERSESSION source imported into #199 as IMPLEMENTED, E10-CMD-106F-TIMELINE implemented and exact-SHA CI green
No product authority reserved choice: HTML is an optional representation, no new permission or persisted object
definition_of_done: Working owner-authorized local browser route from Command Incident Case link, not only JSON/mock unit
Exact candidate SHA passes all three relevant CI workflows and no material blocking R0/R1/R2 defects
Independent L2 on material cross-product data-presentation change before acceptance; native GitHub reviewer approval and merging remain separate

performance_budget.rationale: HTML is a bounded representation of a single already-authorized Case read (default 50 rows; user-provided limit <=200), no new provider read or database, no real production latency measured
